name: MonarchRichTextEditor
title: RichTextEditor
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.text.BasicTextField with a TextFieldValue and a VisualTransformation that draws AnnotatedString SpanStyles from Monarch's own span model, with MonarchEditorToolbar above it and MonarchMentionPicker below it
summary: A rich-text editor on Compose's BasicTextField: a formatting toolbar for bold, italic, strikethrough, code, links, headings and lists, a prompt, a character count against a limit, @mention suggestions and undo, with the document kept as plain text plus spans.
whenToUse: For descriptions, notes, comments and replies that need inline formatting, links, headings or lists.
whenNotToUse: For plain text, use MonarchTextField or a Material 3 OutlinedTextField with several lines. For block documents with tables, callouts and embeds, compose the block components (MonarchTableBlock, MonarchCalloutBlock).
api: @ExperimentalMonarchApi @Composable public fun MonarchRichTextEditor(label: String, state: MonarchRichTextEditorState, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, prompt: String? = null, tools: List<List<MonarchEditorTool>> = MonarchRichTextEditorDefaults.Tools, maxLength: Int? = null, showCharacterCount: Boolean? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, readOnly: Boolean = false, invalid: Boolean = false, mentionItems: List<MonarchMentionItem>? = null, mentionStatus: MonarchMentionPickerStatus = MonarchMentionPickerStatus.Ready, icons: Map<MonarchEditorTool, Painter> = emptyMap(), labels: MonarchRichTextEditorLabels = MonarchRichTextEditorLabels(), onMentionSearch: ((MonarchMentionQuery?) -> Unit)? = null, onMention: ((MonarchMentionItem) -> Unit)? = null, onTool: ((MonarchEditorTool) -> Unit)? = null, interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null)

@Stable public class MonarchRichTextEditorState(text: String = "", spans: List<MonarchRichTextSpan> = emptyList()) { val text: String; val spans: List<MonarchRichTextSpan>; val selection: TextRange; val canUndo: Boolean; val canRedo: Boolean; fun setDocument(text: String, spans: List<MonarchRichTextSpan> = emptyList()); fun undo(); fun redo(); companion object { val Saver: Saver<MonarchRichTextEditorState, Any> } }
@Composable public fun rememberMonarchRichTextEditorState(text: String = "", spans: List<MonarchRichTextSpan> = emptyList()): MonarchRichTextEditorState
public data class MonarchRichTextSpan(mark: MonarchRichTextMark, start: Int, end: Int, url: String? = null)
public enum class MonarchRichTextMark { Bold, Italic, Strikethrough, Code, Link, Heading1, Heading2, Heading3; val isHeading: Boolean }
public object MonarchRichTextEditorDefaults { val Tools: List<List<MonarchEditorTool>>; fun isOverLimit(text: String, maxLength: Int?): Boolean }

public class MonarchRichTextEditorLabels(count: ((Int) -> String)? = null, countOfLimit: ((Int, Int) -> String)? = null, remaining: ((Int) -> String)? = null, over: ((Int) -> String)? = null, toolbar: MonarchEditorToolbarLabels = MonarchEditorToolbarLabels(), mentions: MonarchMentionPickerLabels = MonarchMentionPickerLabels())

options.name: label
options.description: The spoken name of the text area, already localized. Show a visible label nearby, for example with MonarchFormField.

options.name: state
options.description: The document: plain text plus MonarchRichTextSpans, the selection and the undo history. Create it with rememberMonarchRichTextEditorState.

options.name: prompt
options.description: Shown in the subtle text color while the document is empty.

options.name: tools
options.description: The toolbar's tools in groups; emptyList() for no toolbar. Undo, redo, body text, headings 1 to 3, bold, italic, strikethrough, code, link and both lists are applied by the editor; custom tools go to onTool; task lists, quotes, code blocks and headings 4 to 6 are left out.

options.name: maxLength
options.description: The most characters. Typing stops there and a paste is cut to fit; the count shows against it. A longer document set by the app shows the danger count and border.

options.name: showCharacterCount
options.description: Shows the count. By default, shown when there is a maxLength.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the text and the toolbar can be used.

options.name: readOnly
options.description: Shows the document as text, without the toolbar or the box; links open on a tap.

options.name: invalid
options.description: Draws the danger border, for a validation error shown nearby.

options.name: mentionItems
options.description: The suggestions for the mention being typed after @ or #; null turns mentions off.

options.name: mentionStatus
options.description: The state of the mention search: loading, ready or failed.

options.name: icons
options.description: The icons of the toolbar's tools. Monarch bundles no icons: a tool without one shows its name.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the count strings, and the toolbar's and mention picker's labels.

options.name: onMentionSearch
options.description: Receives the mention being typed after @ or #, or null when there is none; search and update mentionItems. Also called by the suggestions' retry.

options.name: onMention
options.description: Receives the chosen person or channel after "@Name " is written into the text.

options.name: onTool
options.description: Receives the custom tools of the toolbar.

options.name: interactionSource
options.description: The interaction source of the text field.

states.name: empty
states.description: The prompt in the subtle text color over the text area.

states.name: focused
states.description: The theme's focus ring around the box while the text or a tool has focus.

states.name: formatting on
states.description: The toolbar toggles of the formats at the caret or over the whole selection are on; the text style menu shows the paragraph's style; a list toggle is on in a list item.

states.name: over the limit
states.description: Only for a longer document set by the app: the count and the border turn the danger color, and the text area's error says how many characters are over.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With enabled = false: the subtle fill and the default border, disabled text, and neither the text nor the toolbar can be used.

states.name: read only
states.description: The document as text, without the box or the toolbar; links are underlined and open on a tap.

states.name: mentioning
states.description: MonarchMentionPicker under the box while @ or # and a name are typed, with its loading, empty and error states.

appearance: A box in the surface color with the input border and medium corners: the toolbar, a subtle divider, then the text in the default text color. Headings use the theme's title, heading and subheading styles, code the code typeface on the muted background, links the link color with an underline. The count is a caption in the muted color, strong danger when over. The roles follow light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web RichTextEditor is built on Tiptap and stores HTML or Tiptap JSON. Compose has no rich-text editor and its styled TextFieldState API sits behind a global foundation flag, so Monarch builds the editor on BasicTextField with a TextFieldValue: the document is plain text plus MonarchRichTextSpans in MonarchRichTextEditorState, which moves the spans with every edit and draws them with a VisualTransformation (the text and offsets are unchanged). iOS binds an AttributedString instead; the Android state is the equivalent, and it stays experimental on both platforms until the interchange format is agreed: no HTML, Markdown or JSON conversion is shipped, and the app stores text and spans. As on iOS: checklists, quotes and code blocks are not offered; lists are text prefixes ("• ", "1. "); headings are levels 1 to 3; a mention is written as plain "@Name " and reported through onMention, where the web inserts a mention node; pasted files are not handled (use MonarchFileUpload beside the editor); the toolbar sits above the text, and the web's toolbarPosition and toolbarEnd are not offered; Markdown typing shortcuts are not offered. Unlike iOS, maxLength stops typing and cuts a paste, as on the web, because the text field reports each change before it is shown. A paste keeps only the plain text, which is the web's safe paste. Undo and redo are the editor's own history of text and formats (100 steps); a hardware keyboard's undo shortcut goes to the text field's own history, which restores text but moves formats only as an edit would. Kotlin-style names: readOnly, invalid and enabled for the iOS isReadOnly, isInvalid and disabled(), showCharacterCount for showsCharacterCount; labels.over is added so the spoken over-the-limit text can be replaced.
accessibility: The text area is a Compose text field whose content description is label, with all system editing actions; past the limit it carries an error, "3 characters over the limit".
The toolbar is MonarchEditorToolbar: a group named "Formatting" whose toggles read their name and on or off state, with 48dp targets; Undo and Redo are disabled when there is nothing to undo or redo.
The count reads "1,988 characters left" or "3 characters over the limit" with a limit, "12 characters" without one, instead of the visible "12 / 2,000".
Mention suggestions are MonarchMentionPicker buttons in a polite live region, so focus can stay in the text.
Formatting is not conveyed by color: bold, italic, strikethrough and headings are type changes, code changes the typeface and links are underlined.
edgeCases: Return at the end of a list item starts the next item (the next number in a numbered list); Return on an empty item ends the list.
Return in a heading splits it into two headings; Return at its end starts body text. Joining a heading to the paragraph before keeps the paragraph's style.

Typing at the end of bold, italic, strikethrough or code continues it; typing after a link does not. A format turned on or off at the caret applies to what is typed next and is dropped when the caret moves.
Characters are counted in UTF-16 units, as String.length, so some emoji count as two.
The undo history is not saved with the state; text, spans and selection are.

examples.title: Document notes
examples.template:
@OptIn(ExperimentalMonarchApi::class)
MonarchRichTextEditor(
    label = {{label}},
    state = state,
    prompt = {{prompt}},
    tools = listOf(
        listOf(MonarchEditorTool.Bold, MonarchEditorTool.Italic, MonarchEditorTool.Strikethrough, MonarchEditorTool.Code),
        listOf(MonarchEditorTool.heading(2), MonarchEditorTool.heading(3)),
        listOf(MonarchEditorTool.BulletList, MonarchEditorTool.OrderedList, MonarchEditorTool.TaskList),
        listOf(MonarchEditorTool.Link, MonarchEditorTool.Blockquote, MonarchEditorTool.CodeBlock),
    ),
)
examples.setupTemplate:
val heading = {{heading}}
val intro = {{intro.before}} + {{intro.bold}} + {{intro.after}} + {{intro.link}} + {{intro.end}}
val boldStart = heading.length + 1 + {{intro.before}}.length
val linkStart = heading.length + 1 + {{intro.before}}.length + {{intro.bold}}.length + {{intro.after}}.length
val doneStart = heading.length + 1 + intro.length + 1 + 2
val state = rememberMonarchRichTextEditorState(
    text = heading + "\n" + intro + "\n\u2611 " + {{tasks.0.label}} + "\n\u2610 " + {{tasks.1.label}} + "\n\u258E " + {{quote}},
    spans = listOf(
        MonarchRichTextSpan(MonarchRichTextMark.Heading2, 0, heading.length),
        MonarchRichTextSpan(MonarchRichTextMark.Bold, boldStart, boldStart + {{intro.bold}}.length),
        MonarchRichTextSpan(MonarchRichTextMark.Link, linkStart, linkStart + {{intro.link}}.length, url = {{intro.href}}),
        MonarchRichTextSpan(MonarchRichTextMark.Strikethrough, doneStart, doneStart + {{tasks.0.label}}.length),
    ),
)
examples.setup:
val heading = "Release checklist"
val intro = "Ship the " + "new onboarding" + " after the review on Thursday. See the " + "rollout guide" + "."
val boldStart = heading.length + 1 + "Ship the ".length
val linkStart = heading.length + 1 + "Ship the ".length + "new onboarding".length + " after the review on Thursday. See the ".length
val doneStart = heading.length + 1 + intro.length + 1 + 2
val state = rememberMonarchRichTextEditorState(
    text = heading + "\n" + intro + "\n\u2611 " + "Update the help article" + "\n\u2610 " + "Tell the support team" + "\n\u258E " + "Keep the old flow behind a setting for one release.",
    spans = listOf(
        MonarchRichTextSpan(MonarchRichTextMark.Heading2, 0, heading.length),
        MonarchRichTextSpan(MonarchRichTextMark.Bold, boldStart, boldStart + "new onboarding".length),
        MonarchRichTextSpan(MonarchRichTextMark.Link, linkStart, linkStart + "rollout guide".length, url = "https://example.com/guide"),
        MonarchRichTextSpan(MonarchRichTextMark.Strikethrough, doneStart, doneStart + "Update the help article".length),
    ),
)
examples.code:
@OptIn(ExperimentalMonarchApi::class)
MonarchRichTextEditor(
    label = "Release notes",
    state = state,
    prompt = "Write notes…",
    tools = listOf(
        listOf(MonarchEditorTool.Bold, MonarchEditorTool.Italic, MonarchEditorTool.Strikethrough, MonarchEditorTool.Code),
        listOf(MonarchEditorTool.heading(2), MonarchEditorTool.heading(3)),
        listOf(MonarchEditorTool.BulletList, MonarchEditorTool.OrderedList, MonarchEditorTool.TaskList),
        listOf(MonarchEditorTool.Link, MonarchEditorTool.Blockquote, MonarchEditorTool.CodeBlock),
    ),
)

parityExceptions.reason: NATIVE GAP: The web document has a heading, bold text, a checklist with one ticked item and a block quote, and the toolbar has the checklist, quote and code block tools. The native editor draws plain text, links and inline marks and the heading mark. A checklist item and the quote are written as lines that start with a check box or a bar glyph, not as real blocks (no check box control, no quote rule, no padding), and the toolbar offers no code block tool. The caret starts at the end of the text, so the quote tool shows as active, where the web has the caret in the heading.
